subject.title: fix(clawhub): SSRF-guard untrusted skill archive download URLs

question: Should OpenClaw formally adopt registry-origin matching as the trust boundary for ClawHub archive URLs, requiring any off-origin archive host to pass the shared public-network SSRF policy?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and proven, but it deliberately changes which self-hosted registry topologies can fetch private off-origin archive hosts; that compatibility-versus-security boundary requires owner intent.

options.title: Adopt the origin boundary
options.body: Accept guarded off-origin downloads and require private archive infrastructure to use the configured registry origin or another policy-compliant host.

options.title: Preserve private mirror support
options.body: Define and document a narrower trusted-mirror configuration or contract before merging, rather than deriving trust from the current auth token.

recommendation.title: Adopt the origin boundary
recommendation.body: Accept guarded off-origin downloads and require private archive infrastructure to use the configured registry origin or another policy-compliant host.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent work owns the same ClawHub archive request lifecycle and makes them the strongest available routing candidate for the combined network contract.
